what: A folder tab attached to the head of each section sticks to both the top of the screen (-1px) and the bottom (0) — tabs of sections not yet reached sit on the bottom row, and tabs of sections already passed stack on the top row, shifted sideways by the width of the previous tab, becoming a table of contents as they are. Tabs overlap their borders by 1px, and the section fills the remaining width of the tab row with the background color so each tab looks like a folder attached to the section head. Motion follows the scroll exactly (sticky) — no curve

options.top: Where the top line sticks (px) — the fixed header’s height if there is one, default 0
options.overlap: Border overlap with adjacent tab (px), default 1
options.[data-fx-part=tab]: Tab (link) placed right before the section — width is the text width (max-content)
options.[data-fx-part=panel]: Section behind the tabs — fills the remaining width of the tab row with the background color

from.where: shared.css .y-tab·.y-panel — header tabs of the four sections Story·Menu·Place·Info (original .tabBtn: position sticky top -1px·bottom 0, left set to the sum of previous tab widths minus the overlapped border, on portrait screens it sticks below the heading height)

note: The original sets the side position with sticky left (relative to the left edge of the screen, so the section must be stuck to the left of the screen to be right). The part shifts with margin-left so it fits wherever it is placed. Tab width is re-measured with ResizeObserver so it stays right even if the font arrives late.
